observed_effect: CONCRETE SELECTOR ADVANTAGE (qualified). Frontier-first selection (37263008074, 37304873966, 37314710995, 37318950814, 37361000967, 37394344201, 37414038601) closed seven distinct frontier cells with decisive, independently verified verdicts and no duplicate recorded retests, whereas the prior opportunistic case (37260572520) took its objective from a queued receipt item and left the process delta UNVERIFIED. The advantage is in recorded research throughput and frontier coverage. It is qualified by a thin opportunistic baseline, an execution-availability confound, and durable-record gaps (two authored-but-unrecorded momentum checks; missing STATE.md sections and activation logs for the cross-sectional-momentum cell and 37394344201; a stale LEARNING_STATE active-delta narrative).
uncertainty_targeted: Whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection produces better information flow than the prior opportunistic task choice.
uncertainty_reduced: Partially reduced: the durable evidence supports a qualified RETAIN of the frontier-first selector; residual uncertainty is causal attribution (thin baseline, execution confound) and whether the authoring layer can be reconciled with the durable record.
research_result: Process audit, not a market test: the frontier-first selector shows a concrete recorded-information-flow advantage over the prior opportunistic choice, but the durable learning layer has an unresolved observability gap (orphaned checks and missing activation logs) that prevents full reconstruction of every completed cell.
next: Retain the frontier-first selector and queue one bounded task to reconcile the authored-but-unrecorded momentum check files against the durable record.
